root.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit: von Popiel Gambit
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5

overview: White pins the knight with 4.Bg5 instead of 4.f3, offering the e4 pawn in a more flexible way. Black can keep the pawn with 4...Bf5 or 4...Nbd7, or hit the bishop with ...h6, and White continues with Nxe4 or g4 for activity. It is a sideline of the Blackmar-Diemer that avoids the main-line f3 theory but also gives Black clear options.

white_ideas.idea: Pressure on f6 and d5, regain the pawn with Nxe4 or Bxf6 and Nxe4 for activity.
Use development and open lines to attack, with g4 or Qe2 ideas against Black's bishop.

black_ideas.idea: Keep the pawn with ...Bf5 or ...Nbd7 and consolidate.

typical_structures.structure: Open game with White d4 against Black pawn on e4 captured; pieces active and files open.

character.notes: Open attacking play with traps, though Black can simplify.

gambit.notes: Black can hold the e4 pawn; White's compensation is activity.

soundness.notes: Dubious like the BDG as a whole; White has not been shown to have enough compensation.

structure.notes: Open lines and files after exchanges on e4.

level.notes: Traps and lines to remember; dubious, so not a first repertoire.

character.reason: Open gambit play with traps and forcing lines.

gambit.reason: White offers e4 which Black can keep.

soundness.reason: Compensation judged insufficient against accurate play.

structure.reason: Open lines and diagonals for pieces.

level.reason: Dubious, so never beginner; a trap-heavy line.

plans.reason: Pawn given for development and activity.
